title: Singleton Init
statement: Implement `solve(levels, guarded)`. `levels` is a list of integer levels passed to successive constructors. `guarded` is 1 when `__init__` runs only the first time the instance is created, and 0 when every constructor call runs `__init__` again on the same object. Return the level that remains. Unguarded, the last level wins. Guarded, the first level wins. An empty list returns `error`.
hints: An empty list has no instance.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: A __new__ singleton that always runs __init__ will reconfigure the shared object on the second constructor call.

editorial: A __new__ singleton that always runs __init__ will reconfigure the shared object on the second constructor call. Guarding init with a flag keeps the first configuration. That bug is why a module-level instance, created once, is easier to reason about than a hand-rolled singleton.
